background: Swedbank is Sweden's largest retail bank by customers and a leading bank in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, funded by Swedish and Baltic deposits and covered bonds and lending mainly on residential mortgages, with the Baltic money-laundering case behind it.
synthesis: The bank is rated AA on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at AA-, all three on a stable outlook, with the last move a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is strong against EU and Nordic peers, with CET1 of 17.4% and leverage of 6.2% both above the peer medians, though both have come down since 30 Jun 2025, CET1 by 2.3 points and leverage by 0.4 points. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 162% above the peer median and NSFR of 122% a little under the median and down 7 points. The newest flagged item, on 27 Jul 2026, is a New York settlement over historical anti-money-laundering failures, closing an old matter rather than opening a new one.
